sections.h2: How a Moses Lake sale works
sections.html:
Three ways to sell exist for a Moses Lake homeowner: hire an agent, go it alone, or deal with a cash buyer who purchases the house in its present condition. No matter which, the paperwork is the same: a deed, a state excise tax affidavit and recording through Grant County.

Moses Lake is the most populous city in Grant County, with an estimated 27,469 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 25,146 in 2020. Owner-occupancy runs 61.2 percent, with a median value of $310,000 for those homes. Median gross rent is $1,216, median household income is $74,752, and the mean trip to work takes 18.2 minutes, which is worth quoting to buyers who commute.

Cash tends to appeal to people with inherited houses, rentals or long repair lists who would rather skip showings and close on a date they pick.

sections.h2: Permits that can trip up a sale
sections.html:
Work done without the permit the city requires is the usual snag. A buyer or title company may ask whether your fence, porch or roof had one, and the Building Department publishes a list of permit types.

ProjectWhen a permit applies
FenceBefore installing any fence
Re-roofWhen it replaces more than 25 percent of the sheathing; solar roof panels also need one
Retaining wallAt 4 feet or higher, measured from the bottom of the footing
Attached covered porchBuilding permit at 200 square feet or more

Remodels, additions and accessory dwelling units go through the city's permit portal with plans, and demolition and grading or clearing each have their own permit. Not sure about a past project? Call the Building Department at 509-764-3743 and ask how an unpermitted structure can be documented before you list.

Nightly rentals need the city's approval, and that approval does not follow the house to a new owner. Chapter 15.650 of the Moses Lake Municipal Code covers stays under 30 days and allows them in specified zoning districts.

An owner applies to the Community Development Department for a short-term rental endorsement, and a business license under Chapter 5.04 is held back until the endorsement is approved. Endorsements are generally not transferable, so a buyer who wants nightly rentals should expect to apply again after closing. If you run the house that way now, tell any buyer the endorsement may not carry over. That also helps you price: an investor counting on nightly income will adjust the offer once they learn the endorsement is not theirs to keep.

The seller files a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit, pays the Grant County Treasurer and then has the deed recorded. Payment falls due on the sale date, which is the notarization date of the deed, even when recording happens afterward.

Through December 31, 2026 the state's graduated rate begins at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 and climbs through 1.28, 2.75 and 3 percent bands. Beginning in 2027 those breakpoints shift upward to $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. A local rate comes on top.

The Grant County Treasurer is at 35 C Street NW, Room 204, in Ephrata, phone 509-754-2010, open weekdays 8 a.m. to noon and 1 to 5 p.m. Ask there how current-year property taxes are handled at your closing; the first half is due April 30.

For improved residential property, RCW 64.06.020 calls for a seller disclosure statement. The buyer should have it five business days after acceptance, though a waiver or an exemption changes that. Answer each line from your own knowledge, mention roof, drainage or permit problems where they apply, and keep a copy with your closing papers. A buyer who finds an undisclosed problem later may come back to you, so err toward writing down what you know. If something has been repaired, say when and by whom, and keep the receipts handy.

Moses Lake has I-90 and State Route 17 bypassing the center, while State Route 171 and I-90 Business serve downtown. Grant Transit Authority runs buses within the city and to Ephrata. Waterfront is plentiful around the lake's three arms, so say so if your house is near the shore. Public schools belong to the Moses Lake School District.

The lake stretches more than 18 miles across its three arms and has over 120 miles of shoreline, so waterfront homes are common here. If yours is one of them, say how close the shore is and what the view looks like, since that drives interest. South of town sit Potholes Reservoir and the Columbia National Wildlife Refuge, a draw for outdoor buyers. The Moses Lake School District runs eleven elementary schools, three middle schools and Moses Lake High School, and buyers with kids will want to confirm assignment for your address.

Plan the last stretch in this order. Sign the deed in front of a notary, because that date sets the excise tax clock. Bring the completed affidavit and payment to the Grant County Treasurer in Ephrata, or have your closing agent do it. After payment clears, the county auditor records the deed.

Do not forget the property tax side. The first half of the year's bill is due April 30, so ask the treasurer what is outstanding and how a prorated share should be handled at closing. A cash buyer will usually let a title company sort this out; on a listing, your escrow officer does.

sections.h2: When cash makes sense in Moses Lake
sections.html:
Consider it if the house needs work, someone still lives in it, or you need a date you can count on. Worn rentals and inherited homes nobody wants to renovate fit well.

Before agreeing to anything, have the buyer confirm funds, commit to a closing day in writing, and spell out who covers excise tax and title costs. A listing eats time with preparation, showings, inspection and a loan; a cash sale closes when you are ready. Request a bid on your address, then hold it up against the leftover from a listing once excise tax, agent fees and repairs are paid.

If you do list, expect the buyer's lender to want the permit and inspection story straight, which is why the Building Department call above comes first.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to sell a Moses Lake house?
faqs.a: Selling itself needs no permit. The city does require permits for work such as fences, re-roofs replacing more than 25 percent of the sheathing, retaining walls of 4 feet or more, and covered porches of 200 square feet or more. If past work lacked a permit, call the Building Department at 509-764-3743 before listing.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax in Moses Lake?
faqs.a: The seller, as a rule. Skip it and the buyer can end up on the hook, with a lien possible. Payment goes to the Grant County Treasurer as of the sale date, and the local rate sits above the state's graduated rate.

faqs.q: Does a short-term rental permit transfer to the buyer in Moses Lake?
faqs.a: Generally no. Endorsements issued under Chapter 15.650 are generally not transferable, so a new owner may need a new endorsement before renting by the night.

faqs.q: How is the excise tax figured on a Moses Lake sale?
faqs.a: State tax opens at 1.1 percent on the lowest slice of the price, with a local rate added. Have your title officer total it before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed and file the excise tax affidavit for a Moses Lake property?
faqs.a: Both go through Grant County. The treasurer takes the excise tax, and state law has deeds recorded with the county auditor. Phone the treasurer at 509-754-2010 to find out what to bring.
